how_read: scripts/kb/fetch_wiki_live_pages.py --api https://cyberpunk.fandom.com/api.php --titles <pages> (page text as rendered by the wiki, link markup removed; the pages are kept in build/wiki-live/cyberpunk-fandom/). Every quoted passage below was checked, by script, to appear word for word in the page text read at the revision named (white space collapsed). A quote that starts 'from the table: ' is a table cell or row of the page (or cells joined in reading order); it appears on the page only once the wiki's table markers are taken out, so a plain word-for-word search will not find it. The wiki also covers the tabletop games and the anime; every page used here describes the video game, and a line states a video-game fact only where the page says so for Cyberpunk 2077. Where a page marks something as needing verification, or mentions an ending or a late quest, the note leaves it out. Quotes are the wiki editors' own sentences or short stat cells; the game's own text on the pages (database entries, scanner and tooltip text, item descriptions) and the artbook passages the wiki quotes are not used.

lines.line: Summary: Arasaka arm blades that count as melee weapons. They deal Physical damage with a 10-20% chance to cause bleeding.

quoted: The Daikon NT Mantis Blades are manufactured by Arasaka.
The Mantis Blades are Cyberware for the Arms in Cyberpunk 2077.
This implant allows you to deal more Physical damage in melee combat, and has a 10-20% chance to apply a Bleed effect.
melee weapons are classified as either Blade, Blunt or Throwable
Bladed weapons include Katanas, Machetes, and the Mantis Blades.

lines.line: Uses: You can leap at enemies in range for a big hit. Each Reflexes point adds 0.5% damage with them.

quoted: While using the Mantis Blades, you can leap to enemies within range to deal massive damage.
Reflexes Attuned +0.5% damage with this cyberware per Attribute Point.

lines.line: Tips: Buy them at a Ripperdoc once you hit level 10; quality rises every 10 levels. The Arms slot holds one cyberware piece, so you pick one arm implant.

quoted: Can be purchased from any Ripperdoc after reaching level 10. Quality increases every 10 levels.
Arms (1 slot)

lines.line: Summary: Arm cyberware that deals Physical damage, with a 10-20% bleed chance and 0.5% more damage per Intelligence point.

quoted: The Monowire is Cyberware for the Arms in Cyberpunk 2077.
Deal Physical damage.
10-20% Bleeding chance
Intelligence Attuned +0.5% damage with this cyberware per Attribute Point.

lines.line: Uses: Its empty slot takes a Control quickhack once you unlock the Jailbreak Relic perk. Charged attacks upload that quickhack to whatever they hit.

quoted: Empty Quickhack Slot
This quickhack will be uploaded to targets that are hit with a charged attack.
With the Jailbreak Relic perk, Control Quickhacks can be installed into a Monowire.

lines.line: Tips: Ripperdocs sell it from level 10; quality rises every 10 levels and tops out at Tier 5. The Arms slot holds one cyberware piece, so you pick one arm implant.

quoted: Can be purchased from any Ripperdoc after reaching level 10. Quality increases every 10 levels, up to Tier 5.
Arms (1 slot)

lines.line: Summary: Arasaka arm cyberware that launches explosive projectiles.

quoted: from the table: Mfr. Arasaka
The Projectile Launch System is Cyberware for the Arms in Cyberpunk 2077.
Projectiles can be charged, and gain 30% increased damage, 25% increased explosion radius and have a 40% increased chance to dismember.

lines.line: Uses: Charge a shot for 30% more damage, 25% more explosion radius and 40% more dismember chance. Each Technical Ability point adds 0.5% damage.

quoted: Projectiles can be charged, and gain 30% increased damage, 25% increased explosion radius and have a 40% increased chance to dismember.
Technical Ability Attuned +0.5% damage with this cyberware per Attribute Point.

lines.line: Tips: Ripperdocs sell it from level 10, and quality rises every 5 levels. The Arms slot holds one cyberware piece, so you pick one arm implant.

quoted: Can be purchased from any Ripperdoc after reaching level 10. Quality increases every 5 levels.
Arms (1 slot)

lines.line: Summary: Arasaka arm cyberware that counts as a blunt melee weapon. It deals Physical damage with a 10-20% chance to cause bleeding.

quoted: from the table: Mfr. Arasaka
The Gorilla Arms are Cyberware for the Arms in Cyberpunk 2077.
This implant allows you to deal more Physical damage in melee combat, and have a 10-20% chance to apply a Bleed effect.
melee weapons are classified as either Blade, Blunt or Throwable
Blunt weapons include Hammers, One and Two-Handed Clubs, Gorilla Arms, and unarmed/bare fists.

lines.line: Uses: Fight in melee with them; each Body point adds 0.5% damage.

quoted: Body Attuned +0.5% damage with this cyberware per Attribute Point.
Blunt weapons include Hammers, One and Two-Handed Clubs, Gorilla Arms, and unarmed/bare fists.

lines.line: Tips: Ripperdocs sell them from level 10, and quality rises every 10 levels. The Arms slot holds one cyberware piece, so you pick one arm implant.

quoted: Can be purchased from any Ripperdoc after reaching level 10. Quality increases every 10 levels.
Arms (1 slot)

lines.line: Summary: Smart weapons steer their bullets onto targets by themselves, but only with the Smart Link cyberware.

quoted: Smart weapons aim for the wielder by using smart rounds that lock on and seek out their targets, though they need to be within the weapons's tracking box.
The Smart Link cyberware is required to enable smart-targeting

lines.line: Uses: Keep the target inside the gun's tracking box. Shots bend around obstacles but fly slower than normal, and you cannot fit a suppressor or scope.

quoted: though they need to be within the weapons's tracking box.
Smart bullets can curve around obstacles to hit their target, but travel slower than conventional rounds.
Smart weapons do not accept either suppressors or scopes.

lines.line: Tips: Smart Link (Hands) adds 10-20% target-lock duration and 5-15% crit damage for Smart weapons from Tier 3. Against Tyger Claws, smart shots miss 50% of the time because of their Masking Ink tattoos.

quoted: The Smart Link is Cyberware for the Hands in Cyberpunk 2077.
At Tier 3 and above it will increase target-lock duration by 10-20% and Crit Damage with Smart Weapons by 5-15%.
Members of the Tyger Claws gang use Masking Ink in their tattoos that jams the smart-targeting ability, giving them a 50% chance to cause smart projectiles to miss.

lines.line: Summary: Railgun-style guns whose shots are driven by an electromagnetic charge.

quoted: Tech weapons are weapons that use railgun technology, firing projectiles that are propelled with an electromagnetic charge.

lines.line: Uses: Charge a shot so it passes through obstacles. Perks for them live under Technical Ability, and using Tech weapons trains the Engineer skill.

quoted: Tech weapons can be charged to fire a bullet capable of penetrating obstacles.
Perks specifically applying to Tech weapons can be found in the Technical Ability Attribute, and utilizing Tech weapons grants experience for the Engineer skill.

lines.line: Tips: You cannot attach a suppressor to a Tech weapon, but most let you add a custom sight.

quoted: Tech weapons cannot be fitted with a suppressor, but most of them accept a custom sight.

lines.line: Summary: Your Neuroport takes this datashard, which is what lets you quickhack and run Breach Protocol. Without a deck you cannot start Breach Protocol.

quoted: cyberdecks have evolved to be a type of datashard that is installed in one's Neuroport system, and allows its users to perform Netrunner abilities, such as quickhacks and Breach Protocol.
thus a cyberdeck is mandatory in order to make use of Breach Protocol.

lines.line: Uses: Quickhacks spend RAM. Buffer size caps the Code Matrix characters you can pick in Breach, and better decks have bigger ones.

quoted: In order to perform quickhacks, you require base RAM.
The buffer size is used during Breach Protocol, and determines the amount of characters you can select from the Code Matrix.
The buffer size can be increased by equipping higher quality cyberdecks.

lines.line: Tips: Spent RAM returns after 60 seconds outside combat. Quickhacking perks and Frontal Cortex cyberware change your RAM, and resistant enemies cost more to hack.

quoted: Once a RAM unit has been used, it will take 60 seconds outside of combat to recover.
can be modified by perks in the Quickhacking skill tree in the Intelligence attribute or by installing Frontal Cortex cyberware.
Certain enemies may have quickhack resistance, increasing the amount of base RAM required for them to be hacked.

lines.line: Summary: Two healing consumables: the Trauma Team MaxDoc inhaler and the Bounce Back injector.

quoted: The MaxDoc is an inhaler manufactured by Trauma Team.
from the table: Type Injector

lines.line: Uses: The MaxDoc heals 50-126 Health when used. The Bounce Back heals 10-30 at once, then 6-17 more every second for 10 seconds.

quoted: It allows the user to restore 50-126 Health when used.
The Bounce Back allows the user to instantly restore 10-30 Health, and then regenerating an additional 6-17 Health per second for 10 seconds.

lines.line: Tips: You can find both in caches and on enemies. Vendors sell the MaxDoc, Meds Vendors sell the Bounce Back, and your inventory stacks them to 150.

quoted: Can be acquired from caches, Enemies, and Vendors.
Can be acquired from caches, Enemies, and Meds Vendors.
These items have a max stack of 150 in your inventory

lines.line: Summary: Enemy netrunners use quickhacks. The Voodoo Boys Netrunner (Tier 2) uses Cyberware Malfunction, Reboot Optics, Ping and Overheat.

quoted: The Netrunner is a Tier 2 enemy affiliated with the Voodoo Boys in Cyberpunk 2077.
*Uses the Cyberware Malfunction, Reboot Optics and Ping quickhacks.
from the table: Netrunner Overheat Charge Jump

quoted: A Tier 1 combat quickhack that sets the enemy on fire, dealing Thermal damage over time.
EMP Grenades

3-6 Tier 3 Quickhack Components
3-5 Tier 4 Quickhack Components

lines.line: Summary: Robots, mechs and drones always have to be destroyed. Human foes can be subdued without killing them.

quoted: human enemies can be taken down both lethally or non-lethally, while robots, mechs, and drones can only be destroyed.

lines.line: Tips: An enemy's icon colour shows its threat: white or grey is very low, and red is very high.

quoted: Enemies' threat levels are indicated by the color of their enemy type icon, within the yellow border, ranging from white/ grey (very low threat), through green, yellow, orange, up to red (very high threat).

lines.line: Summary: One of Night City's largest gangs, based in Japantown but also holding ground in Westbrook and Watson.

quoted: During the 2070s, the Tyger Claws were a ruthless territorial gang based in Japantown.
During the 2070s, the Tyger Claws were one of the largest criminal groups in Night City, controlling vast swaths of land in Westbrook and Watson.

lines.line: Looks like: Glowing tattoos and katanas mark them out.

quoted: Tyger foot soldiers were easily recognized by their Asian luminous tattoos, fast street bikes, katanas, and tantos.

lines.line: Tips: Their Masking Ink tattoos make smart-weapon shots miss 50% of the time. Its Hunter is a melee enemy at Tier 2; the gang also uses reflex boosters and pain editors.

quoted: Members of the Tyger Claws gang use Masking Ink in their tattoos that jams the smart-targeting ability, giving them a 50% chance to cause smart projectiles to miss.
The Hunter is a Tier 2 enemy affiliated with the Tyger Claws in Cyberpunk 2077.
from the table: Type Melee
Cyberware used by the gang included reflex boosters, augmented cyberlimbs, pain editors, and electronic countermeasures (ECM) systems disguised as tattoos.

lines.line: Summary: A boostergang controlling much of Watson's Northside Industrial District. Its Goon (ranged or melee) and Ironstormer (heavy ranged) are both Tier 2.

quoted: Maelstrom was a dangerous, violent boostergang
They controlled much of the Northside Industrial District in Watson, but their influence extended further south.
The Goon is a Tier 2 enemy affiliated with Maelstrom in Cyberpunk 2077.
The Goon can either be a Ranged or a Melee enemy.
The Ironstormer is a Tier 2 enemy affiliated with Maelstrom in Cyberpunk 2077.
from the table: Type Heavy Ranged

lines.line: Looks like: Chrome-heavy bodies and occult-style tattoos, looking more machine than human.

quoted: Their physical appearance was distinguished by their dehumanizing heavy cyberware augmentations and occult-inspired tattoos.
No one joined them without undergoing an extensive cyberware implantation that not only changed their looks to appear less human and more machine-like, but also enhanced their bodies.

lines.line: Tips: Ranged Goons carry frag grenades. The Ironstormer also wears Medium Subdermal Armor.

quoted: The Goon can either be a Ranged or a Melee enemy.
Ranged
Frag Grenades
Medium Subdermal Armor

lines.line: Summary: Scavs kidnap people and take their cyberware by force. You can meet them all over Night City.

quoted: They are known for kidnapping people and forcibly harvesting their cyberware.
Scavengers can be found all over Night City.

lines.line: Looks like: Tracksuits and Soviet cyberware give them away.

quoted: Scavengers are recognized by their tracksuits, Soviet cyberware, and criminal tattoos.

lines.line: Tips: Vultures are Tier 2 heavy ranged Scavs, equipped with frag grenades and Medium Subdermal Armor.

quoted: The Vulture is a Tier 2 enemy affiliated with the Scavengers in Cyberpunk 2077.
from the table: Type Heavy Ranged
from the table: Frag Grenades Medium Subdermal Armor Charge Jump

lines.line: Summary: The NCPD's cyberpsycho hunters come for you at five wanted stars, the last enemy type to do so. On higher difficulties a few shots can kill you at any level.

quoted: At some point during or after the Time of the Red, MAX-TAC was reincorporated into the NCPD.
In 2077, MaxTac continued to live up to their reputation, hunting down any cyberpsychos and lawbreakers too powerful for the regular officers to handle.
reaching a maximum wanted rating (five stars) will result in the deployment MaxTac officers, who serve as the final enemy type to hunt V down while wanted.
On higher difficulties, they are capable of killing V in just a few shots regardless of character level.

lines.line: Tips: Squads have four officers, each in one of these roles: Assault, Mantis, Heavy, Netrunner or Sniper. Mantis officers have the second highest armor, and officers often use Sandevistan Mk.3 and Kerenzikov.

quoted: MaxTac officers operate in squads of four each and contain an operator for each of four different roles:
Assault - Frontline fighters who utilize the Ajax and Defender.
Mantis - Close-quarter specialists who utilize MaxTac-built mantis blades and the Omaha as backup weapons. They hold the second highest armor rating.
Heavy - Walking tanks in exosuits who utilize the Defender to dish out large amounts of damage in seconds.
Netrunner - Field hackers who typically avoid direct combat in favor of utilizing quickhacks that are slow to upload, but cause high amounts of damage.
Sniper - Long-range specialists armed with the Ashura to attack V from a distance. These officers make significantly more use of their Sandevistan.
For cyberware, officers make regular use of Sandevistan Mk. 3 and Kerenzikov.
